To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a 3D stacked SPAD image sensor capable of SPC intensity and time resolved imaging with a 7.83 µm pitch, the lowest reported to date.
we present the first BSI 3D stacked CMOS SPAD image sensor.
we present a 3D-staked BSI SPAD image sensor capable of single-photon counting and time-resolved imaging with a pixel pitch of only 7.83 µm, the smallest reported for any SPAD image sensor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of 3D stacked SPAD image sensors with high spatial resolution and low power consumption.
the development of a new generation of image sensors based on single photon avalanche diodes (SPAD).
the development of a new type of image sensor based on a single photon avalanche diodes (SPADs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented 3D-stacking technology is a promising approach to realize a high performance SPAD image sensor.
the 3D-stacking approach is very suitable for the development of high resolution SPAD imagers, and the 3D SPAD sensor presented is the smallest SPAD image sensor reported to date.
the 3D-stacking of SPADs in BSI configuration has been demonstrated for the first time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPAD has the smallest pixel size, lowest DCR and highest PDP of any reported SPAD image sensor.
we were able to achieve a very low dark count rate, and a high PDP in the same SPAD.
this is the first 3-D stacked backside illuminated SPAD imager.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of 3D-stacking technology allows for a significant reduction in the pixel pitch of SPADs, which is a key enabler for the development of high resolution SPAD imagers for applications such as fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), single photon lidar (SPL), single molecule localization microscopy (SMLM), and single photon counting (SCC) imaging.

a 3D-stacking approach can provide the required performance and scalability for SPAD image sensor technology, and can potentially enable the integration of SPAD arrays with high speed readout and processing electronics.
the 3D-stacking of CMOS technology enables a high performance, small pixel SPAD image sensor that is capable of high resolution, low noise, time-resolved imaging.
